children: ), the open-source, China-based AI startup, released a new model today, V4.1-Flash, which offers tokens at a much discounted price compared to its U.S. counterparts.

It also requires just a fraction of the high-bandwidth memory and solid-state drive storage requirements, the startup said. The new model presents a fresh challenge for U.S. frontier labs such as OpenAI

A growing number of U.S. companies have already adopted the use of China-based open AI models due to the cost savings. In late 2025, U.S. models consumed roughly 80% of tokens among the top 50 AI models, while Chinese models accounted for under 20%, according to BCA Chief Economist
. By August 2026, those figures flipped, with Chinese models claiming more than 60% of token consumption and U.S. models falling below 40%.
At the same time, U.S. intelligence agencies have alleged that major Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI, are systematically
proprietary data from American models to train their models.

"Introducing the smallest model in our new architecture family, with native visual understanding," DeepSeek said in a post on X on Thursday. "Designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput, and scaling to larger models."

The 552B-parameter model utilizes a new causal encoder-decoder architecture that only uses 8B active parameters for input and 16B for output. Compared to its previous generation, V4.1-Flash's KV cache requires one-fourth the amount of HBM and one-eighth the amount of SSD storage, the startup said.
The new model is available now via the DeepSeek API.

V4.1-Flash surpassed Anthropic's Opus 5 and OpenAI's GPT 5.6-Sol in certain benchmarks, according to data provided by DeepSeek. This included DeepSWE v1.1, CyberGym and Automation-Bench. However, Anthropic's and OpenAI's models surpassed V4.1-Flash in the Terminal Bench 3.0.

title: DeepSeek's new ultra-low-cost model presents challenges for US frontier labs
